purpose: Editorially selected Signals candidates for the Sunday 27 September 2026 edition. The choices favour specific primary-source developments that put an external model, provider, market safeguard or exploitable component directly into a decision path; routine status notices and isolated cases were not promoted.

topics.editorialRationale: Select Anthropic's Project Swap research because agents transacting on a user's behalf makes permission, intervention and evidence part of the trading boundary rather than a product-design detail.
Select ASIC's AI trading safeguards because they make market integrity a deployment and oversight question for automated activity, not a separate policy consideration.

Select the Bank of England's fees regime because recognised payment systems and specified service providers are being supervised as operationally material parts of the payment chain, rather than treated as an external backdrop.
Select ENISA's dependency analysis because it connects digital resilience to the practical chain of suppliers and services on which a firm can no longer assume isolation.
No fresh financial-crime candidate cleared the threshold. The available cases do not change a firm-wide control decision; retain reviewed material.
Select CISA's newly catalogued exploited vulnerabilities because an alert is only useful when affected external components and their owners can be found and contained quickly.
No new technology-failure notice cleared the materiality threshold. Retain the reviewed dependency records rather than elevate raw operational status copy.
No fresh data candidate cleared the threshold. Retain reviewed material rather than elevate a generic publication.
